newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Suharto said to favor equity limit.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto said to favor equity limit.

text.p: President Suharto was quoted as saying on Tuesday that individual shareholdings should not exceed 15 percent in companies listed on Indonesia's stock exchanges.

"The control should not exceed 15 percent. It should be a maximum of 15 percent and other people should be able to get a stake," Subiyakto Tjakrawerdaya, the minister of cooperatives and small business, quoted Suharto as saying.
The minister's comments followed a meeting with the president to discuss the development of cooperatives and small businesses.
Suharto's view was that an individual shareholding in a private Indonesian company going public should in general not exceed 15 percent, the minister said.
He said Suharto wanted "equitability" in shareholdings, and that this was his commitment to the public.
Tjakrawerdaya gave no indication that the government had any plans to restrict shareholdings or make provision for retroactive rulings.

The minister declined to name any specific company, but it appeared from the context he was referring in particular to the issue of Indonesia's largest car maker, Astra International, which had been the target of a bidding war in recent weeks.
Brokers said in late October that business interests close to Suharto were believed to have picked up sizeable holdings in Astra.

They said the Nusamba group, 80 percent owned by three charitable foundations headed by the president, and the Salim group, controlled by close Suharto associate Liem Sioe Liong, could be holding shares representing a 30 percent stake in Astra. The actual holdings remained unclear, however, brokers said.
Tjakrawerdaya said there was no problem with government holdings in a state company floated on the exchange "because it is owned by the people".

An analyst from a local securities firm said restricting the level of shareholdings would enhance liquidity on the stock market, and would enhance the competitiveness of Indonesian bourses in Southeast Asia.
"From an investor's point of view, a stock becomes very liquid if it belongs to many parties," he said.
